rationale: WIN-055 (Cepheid/SBF distance-redshift) detail_evidence currently claims TRGB "converging with Cepheid and SBF results within measurement uncertainty." That overstates the H0 consensus: the ~5σ Cepheid/SH0ES (~73 km/s/Mpc) vs TRGB/CCHP (~69.8) tension is well-known and persistent in the 2024-2026 literature. A motivated cosmology-aware reader can dismiss our review as careless for this line. The fix preserves our actual argument — that all three rungs agree on the *distance ladder* itself (calibrated galaxy distances at 10-100 Mpc) — and narrowly carves out that the H0 *tension* concerns the expansion rate inferred from those distances, not the existence of the ladder. The dome refutation argument is unaffected: dome has no ladder of any slope.

prose_patches.old: yields H₀ = 69.8 ± 1.9 km/s/Mpc (Freedman et al. 2019, CCHP, ApJ 882, 34), converging with Cepheid and SBF results within measurement uncertainty.
prose_patches.new: yields H₀ = 69.8 ± 1.9 km/s/Mpc (Freedman et al. 2019, CCHP, ApJ 882, 34). Cepheid, TRGB, and SBF measurements agree to within roughly 1-2% on individual galaxy distances at 10-100 Mpc; the well-known ~5σ H₀ tension between SH0ES Cepheid-anchored (~73 km/s/Mpc) and CCHP TRGB-anchored (~69.8) values concerns the expansion rate inferred from those distances, not the existence of the distance ladder itself.

kernel_of_truth.description: The 2019 framing — that TRGB, Cepheid, and SBF "converge within measurement uncertainty" — was reasonable shorthand at the time the tension was 3-4σ and considered possibly statistical. The text was likely fine when written. What changed is the field: the tension is now persistent and structural (~5σ across multiple independent analyses through 2024-2025).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_matters: We are not catching a mathematical error — we are catching a stylistic gloss that has aged. The Freedman et al. 2019 paper itself framed CCHP-TRGB as consistent with SH0ES within their own quoted uncertainties; we inherited the framing.
